role: Supporting methodology only. Static publications and dated snapshots are excluded from the current-news feed.

families.name: GPQA / GPQA Diamond
families.measures: Multiple-choice performance on expert-written graduate-level biology, chemistry and physics questions. Main GPQA has 448 questions; Diamond is a higher-quality 198-question subset filtered using expert/non-expert validation.
families.usefulness_inference: A useful signal for difficult specialized scientific question answering and reasoning; it is not a complete test of general assistant quality or research competence.
families.limitations: Small and specialized; the paper disclaims representativeness of scientific questions and notes limited statistical power for small accuracy differences. Do not compare main-set and Diamond percentages as the same test.

families.name: IFEval
families.measures: Adherence to verifiable output constraints such as word limits, keyword inclusion, response language and JSON formatting. Original set contains 541 prompts and 25 instruction types.
families.usefulness_inference: A practical signal for workflows that require specific format and constraint compliance; compliance scores do not independently validate whether the requested content is true or useful.
families.limitations: Four metrics exist: prompt-level or instruction-level, each strict or loose. Prompt-level requires all constraints in a prompt. Loose scoring transforms responses to reduce false negatives and can introduce false positives. Authors acknowledge limited instruction diversity and need for more realistic and multimodal tasks.

families.name: LiveBench
families.measures: A broad suite with objective ground-truth scoring across math, coding, reasoning, language, instruction following and data analysis, designed to use refreshed recent source material.
families.usefulness_inference: Helps triangulate abilities across categories while reducing dependence on an LLM judge; category scores are more informative for a specific task than an aggregate alone.
families.limitations: Release and harness changes affect comparability. Changelog documents coding-agent replacement and increased step limit in October 2025, illustrating that scores can change with the environment. Latest rendered changelog entry retrieved today is 2026-01-08, so monthly updates through October 2026 were not established.

families.name: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL)
families.measures: Tool/function calling correctness: selection, arguments and relevance, with version-specific single-turn, multi-turn and agentic tests. V4 extends evaluation with web search, memory and format sensitivity.
families.usefulness_inference: Relevant to assistants that interact with APIs and take multiple steps; a tool-calling score is not certification that a deployed agent is dependable in every environment.
families.limitations: Version and category matter. AST evaluation checks call structure; multi-turn evaluations inspect states and required result paths. Real application behavior also depends on tool definitions, orchestration and environment. Avoid treating all BFCL versions as one identical metric.

families.name: Long context: NIAH / RULER / LongBench v2
families.measures: Needle-in-a-haystack checks retrieval of specific embedded information. RULER broadens synthetic checks to multiple retrieval variants, multi-hop tracing, aggregation and question answering while varying input length and complexity. LongBench v2 uses realistic long-context multiple-choice problems across six domains.
families.usefulness_inference: Distinguishes the advertised input window from successful use of content. Long-document work requires understanding and combining evidence beyond finding one fact.
families.limitations: RULER authors explicitly say synthetic behavioral checks should not be preferred over realistic tasks; they did not establish real-task correlation and comprehensive prompt robustness. LongBench v2 multiple-choice scoring does not independently test every aspect of free-form synthesis.
